summary: Vellacombe describes how Route scout and delivery converts a chemical hypothesis into a route-gate decision and an agreed delivery lot. Impurity isolation and Analogue preparation are presented with explicit limits on proposed structures, isolated material and analytical assignment.

properties.title: Route scout and delivery
properties.subject: Vellacombe chemistry capabilities
properties.keywords: route scout; delivery; impurity isolation; analogue preparation

Route-risk decisions, impurity isolation and Analogue preparation

slides.title: Begin with the chemistry question
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: State the desired structure and the decision the material will support.
Separate a plausible disconnection from a route demonstrated on isolated material.
Agree the route gate before committing to a wider analogue set.

slides.title: Route scout and delivery
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Compare competing disconnections and access to the key intermediate.
Identify the transformation most likely to prevent delivery.
Carry a demonstrated route into an agreed delivery lot.

slides.title: Define the request
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Confirm connectivity, stereochemistry and the required delivery form.
Review starting material access and handling constraints.
Discuss prior attempts and unresolved assignments.
Agree the evidence needed to continue, redirect or stop.

slides.title: Test the weakest assumption
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Use diagnostic experiments to distinguish substrate failure from condition failure.
Examine selectivity and downstream compatibility.
Record unsuccessful transformations when they change the route choice.
Keep proposed intermediates separate from isolated compounds.

slides.title: Make the route gate explicit
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Uncertain bond formation: establish the desired product before continuing.
Difficult isolation: change work-up or reconsider the route.
Unstable intermediate: assess handling before committing to delivery.
Stereochemical ambiguity: resolve the requirement before wider preparation.

slides.title: From reaction to delivery
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: An analytical signal is a lead for isolation.
Check that work-up and purification remain practical as material demand changes.
Record isolated yield against the compound card and experiment.
Resolve identity and purity before release.

slides.title: Impurity isolation
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Start from the observed impurity and the question it raises.
Choose enrichment or separation conditions that preserve the species of interest.
Distinguish the original impurity from a product formed during handling.
Retain evidence of the source material in the chemistry note.

slides.title: Assignment has limits
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Use available characterisation to support connectivity and stereochemistry.
State ambiguity where the evidence does not distinguish alternatives.
A proposed impurity structure remains proposed until supported.
Do not equate enrichment with isolation or isolation with complete assignment.

slides.title: Analogue preparation
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Define the structural change that tests the chemical hypothesis.
Use shared intermediates where the chemistry supports them.
Feed observed reactivity back into selection of the next analogue.
Keep unsuccessful preparations visible in the chemistry note.

slides.title: Compound cards preserve the evidence
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Distinguish proposed targets from assigned isolated material.
Link attempted conditions and demonstrated preparations to the relevant experiment.
Report mass in mg, amount in mmol where applicable and purity in area percent.
State what the evidence supports and what remains unresolved.

slides.title: Release is a chemistry decision
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Clara Fenwick, Analytical Release Lead, coordinates the analytical release review.
Identity, purity and delivery form must match the agreed request.
Raise unresolved impurities or assignments before material is released.
The chemistry note records the release decision and agreed limitations.

slides.title: A handover for the next experiment
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Link the delivery lot to its compound card and characterisation.
Describe the critical transformations and practical handling constraints.
Carry forward impurity and stability observations relevant to use.
Recommend the next analogue or route gate.

slides.title: Next discussion: structure, risk, route gate
slides.footer: Vellacombe Discovery Ltd, a Tarnovell company | Confidential
bullets: Bring the target structure, prior chemistry and intended use.
Agree whether the initial question needs Route scout and delivery, impurity isolation or Analogue preparation.
Confirm delivery requirements with Dr R. Calderwood.
Leave with an explicit hypothesis and the evidence required to act on it.
